message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide for pulling “detailed” interface data on the three most common desktop/server operating systems (Linux, Windows, macOS). If you’re working with a different platform (e.g., embedded firmware, a virtual appliance, or a cloud‑managed switch), let me know and I’ll tailor the instructions accordingly. --- ## 1️⃣ Linux / Unix‑like Systems | Tool | What it shows | Typical command | |------|---------------|-----------------| | **`ip`** | Interface state, MAC, MTU, IPs, flags, queue lengths | `ip link show eth0` | | **`ifconfig`** *(deprecated but still present)* | Same as above plus broadcast address | `ifconfig eth0` | | **`ethtool`** | Driver name, firmware version, speed/duplex, autonegotiation status, statistics counters, supported features | `ethtool -i eth0` (driver)
`ethtool -S eth0` (stats)
`ethtool -a eth0` (autoneg) | | **`ethtool -T`** | Link training status (for 10G/40G NICs) | `ethtool -T eth0` | | **`ethtool -P`** | Permanent MAC address | `ethtool -P eth0` | | **`ethtool -m`** | EEPROM contents (useful for firmware checks) | `ethtool -m eth0` | | **`lshw -class network`** | Full hardware description (bus info, vendor, product ID, configuration) | `sudo lshw -class network -short` | | **`dmidecode -t 9`** | BIOS/firmware version for NIC (if supported) | `sudo dmidecode -t 9` | | **`sysfs`** (`/sys/class/net//`) | Low‑level sysfs attributes (e.g., `/sys/class/net/eth0/device/modalias`) | `cat /sys/class/net/eth0/device/modalias` | | **SNMP** | Standard MIB data (IF-MIB, HOST-RESOURCES-MIB) | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifTable` | ### Quick example – gather everything at once ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash IF=eth0 echo "=== ip link ===" ip link show $IF echo "=== ethtool -i ===" ethtool -i $IF echo "=== ethtool -S ===" ethtool -S $IF echo "=== lshw ===" sudo lshw -class network -short | grep "$IF" echo "=== sysfs modalias ===" cat /sys/class/net/$IF/device/modalias ``` Run this script as root (or with `sudo`) to pull all the low‑level details in one shot. --- ## 2️⃣ Windows (PowerShell) | Cmdlet | What it shows | Typical command | |--------|---------------|-----------------| | **`Get-NetAdapter`** | Adapter name, status, MAC, speed, duplex, driver, firmware | `Get-NetAdapter -Name Ethernet | Format-List *` | | **`Get-NetIPConfiguration`** | IP addresses, DNS servers, gateway | `Get-NetIPConfiguration -InterfaceAlias Ethernet | Format-List *` | | **`Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty`** | Advanced settings (e.g., Jumbo Frame, RSS) | `Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name Ethernet | Format-Table Name, DisplayName, DisplayValue` | | **`Get-NetAdapterStatistics`** | Packet counters, errors, collisions | `Get-NetAdapterStatistics -Name Ethernet | Format-Table *` | | **`Get-NetAdapterHardwareInfo`** | Vendor, product ID, firmware version | `Get-NetAdapterHardwareInfo -Name Ethernet | Format-List *` | | **`Get-WmiObject Win32_NetworkAdapter`** | Raw WMI data (including PNPDeviceID) | `Get-WmiObject Win32_NetworkAdapter -Filter "NetConnectionID='Ethernet'" | Format-List *` | | **`Get-CimInstance MSFT_NetAdapter`** | CIM equivalent (recommended over legacy WMI) | `Get-CimInstance MSFT_NetAdapter -Filter "Name='Ethernet'" | Format-List *` | ### Example PowerShell snippet ```powershell $adapter = Get-NetAdapter -Name Ethernet $adapter | Format-List * Get-NetIPConfiguration -InterfaceAlias Ethernet | Format-List * Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name Ethernet | Format-Table Name, DisplayName, DisplayValue Get-NetAdapterStatistics -Name Ethernet | Format-Table * Get-NetAdapterHardwareInfo -Name Ethernet | Format-List * ``` Run the script in an elevated PowerShell session (Run as Administrator). --- ## 3️⃣ macOS | Command | What it shows | Typical usage | |---------|---------------|---------------| | **`ifconfig`** | Interface state, MAC, IP, flags, MTU | `ifconfig en0` | | **`networksetup -getinfo`** | Service name, IP, subnet mask, router, DNS servers | `networksetup -getinfo Wi-Fi` | | **`networksetup -listallhardwareports`** | Mapping between service names and physical ports | `networksetup -listallhardwareports` | | **`system_profiler SPNetworkDataType`** | Detailed hardware info (vendor, product, firmware) | `system_profiler SPNetworkDataType | grep -A5 "en0:"` | | **`scutil --dns`** | System DNS resolver config | `scutil --dns` | | **`netstat -i`** | Interface statistics (bytes, packets, errors) | `netstat -i` | | **`ethtool`** (via Homebrew) | Same as Linux if installed | `brew install ethtool && sudo ethtool -i en0` | ### Quick macOS example ```bash #!/bin/bash IF=en0 echo "=== ifconfig ===" ifconfig $IF echo "=== networksetup ===" networksetup -getinfo Wi-Fi echo "=== system_profiler ===" system_profiler SPNetworkDataType | grep -A7 "$IF:" ``` --- ## 📌 Common Pitfalls & Tips | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **Permission denied** | Run commands as root (Linux/macOS) or with `sudo`; run PowerShell as Administrator. | | **Missing `ethtool`** | Install via package manager (`apt-get install ethtool`, `yum install ethtool`, `brew install ethtool`). | | **Wrong interface name** | Use `ip link` (Linux), `Get-NetAdapter` (Windows), or `networksetup -listallhardwareports` (macOS) to list available adapters. | | **Driver not loaded** | Check `dmesg` or `journalctl -k` for kernel messages; load module with `modprobe ` (Linux). | | **Firmware not exposed** | Some NICs expose firmware via `/sys/class/net//device/firmware_version` (Linux) or via WMI/SMBIOS tables. | --- ## 🎯 TL;DR 1. **Linux** – `ip link show `, `ethtool -i `, `ethtool -S `, `lshw -class network`. 2. **Windows** – `Get-NetAdapter -Name | Format-List *`, `Get-NetIPConfiguration`, `Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty`. 3. **macOS** – `ifconfig `, `networksetup -getinfo `, `system_profiler SPNetworkDataType`. Feel free to copy/paste the snippets into your terminal or PowerShell window. If you hit a snag (e.g., missing command, permission error, or you’re on a different OS), just let me know!
